notes: v2.121 (2026-11-20, late run): 120th tower 'Advent Calendar' (a roof over three window bands on a split base — a house-shaped advent-calendar silhouette to demolish, 35 blocks, 6 clusters sizes 3/3/7/7/7/8, all 4 colours, no singletons, 0 canonical duplicates) + 117th co-play prompt (open one door together — a grown-up tapes 5 little paper doors on a big piece of paper, or use a real advent calendar; each morning Liam opens one door saying 'open… ta-da!', finds a little surprise behind it, and counts the doors opened so far — one, two, three!; at 2 the game is just open and find — no rules, no counting to 24, no little sweets or small treats behind the doors). Advent calendar research: one door a day is anticipation in tiny daily doses — opening a door is fine-motor work (grasp, pull a tab) and the surprise behind it is the payoff; toddler calendars use big refillable bins/doors (18mo+); counting is counting the first few doors together, not to 24.
